motivation.observedNativeFailure: The b5 iPhone artifact shows blank cover artwork with closed-book controls, then a later screenshot shows the first page. The published entry handler waits for native animation completion before opening. That supports the handoff weakness but does not timestamp a callback or establish its scheduler cause. The device flow did not reach Next/Previous page turning.
motivation.separateControlledReproduction: The actual MemoryPageTurn component also waits indefinitely for native completion: withheld callbacks strand a tap, committed swipe and cancelled swipe. Additional controlled tests reproduce completion between an inactive/size/reduced-motion/unmount commit and passive cleanup, plus a delimiter collision in content identity. These eight controlled failures are not eight observed device failures.

changes: Retain the existing memoryTurnDuration and visual native animation; a JavaScript timer at that same intended duration can finish settlement when native completion is missing.
Timer and native completion share first-result disposal. Retire callback ownership and the timer before stopping native work, whose interruption callback can be synchronous.
Keep machine token and live checks; retain the committed turn lock until React acknowledges its selected index.
Cancel settlement in layout-phase identity, active-state, geometry, reduced-motion and unmount handling, before passive-effect cleanup can lag behind another completion.
Use JSON-encoded content identity: equal fresh arrays preserve the turn, while distinct IDs containing delimiters invalidate old work.
Keep one live media child, static preview behavior, user interruption/cancel semantics and immediate reduced-motion navigation.

publishedCounterfactual.method: Final frozen test file executed unchanged; a controlled local fs.readFileSync preloader substitutes only the exact component path with literal published b5 bytes. No checkout source or installed dependency is changed.

verification.testModel: Actual transpiled React component and shared machine execute with controlled hook/native hosts, a deterministic JS clock and explicitly deferred passive cleanup. Native animation completion can be delivered, withheld or late.

limits: A JS timer bounds settlement once JavaScript can run; it cannot guarantee a wall-clock deadline while the JS thread is blocked or suspended.
